memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now no shrub had yet appeared on the earth and no plant had yet sprung up, for the Lord God had not sent rain on the earth and there was no one to work the ground, but streams came up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground. Then the Lord God formed a man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being. — Gen 2:5–7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The scene opens on an earth that is waiting. The plants of the field had not yet sprung up, and one reason given is striking: there was no one to work the ground. Creation was ready, but something—someone—was still to come. Then God acts, and the way He makes man is deeply personal.

Notice the difference. God spoke the stars, seas, and creatures into being with a word. But when He made man, He stooped down. He formed him, like a potter shaping clay with his own hands, from the humble dust of the ground. Then He drew close and breathed into him the breath of life. We are not accidents flung into existence. We are handmade by God, given life by His very breath.

This holds two truths together beautifully. We are humble—made of dust, and to dust our bodies return (Gen 3:19). Yet we are precious—carrying the breath of the living God. Never let anyone tell you your life is small or meaningless. The hands that shaped the mountains also shaped you.

And there is more. The first Adam received natural life from God's breath; in Christ, the last Adam, we receive eternal life by His Spirit (1 Cor 15:45). The God who formed you longs to make you fully alive in Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How does knowing you were personally formed by God change the way you see yourself?
- Do you hold together both your humility (dust) and your worth (God's breath)?
- What would it mean to receive the fuller life Christ offers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that I am not an accident but formed by Your own hands and given life by Your breath. When I feel small, remind me of Your care, and make me fully alive in Christ. Amen.
